newsitem.title: INDIA: India ASSOCHAM wants 15 pct limit on FI holdings.
newsitem.headline: India ASSOCHAM wants 15 pct limit on FI holdings.

text.p: India's leading industry body on Tuesday asked the government to limit the holdings of financial institutions to 15 percent of the equity of a company.

In a memorandum to Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda the Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry (ASSOCHAM) asked the government to clearly demarcate the role of financial institutions (FIs) and the extent of their holdings in Indian firms.
"This is necessary to impart liquidity to the market and reduce exposure of management to decisions of FIs," it stated.
The memorandum was submitted ahead of the federal budget for 1997/98 (April-March) which is due to be presented next month.

"To bring down the holdings of FIs to 15 percent within a reasonable time, the FI should sell three percent of the equity every year to the managements at market price until the latter controls 51 percent," the statement said.
ASSOCHAM suggested banks should let promoters buy shares on soft terms against a pledge of shares.
The industry body recommended that in the case of a hostile takeover of a professional company the financial institutions should back the existing management.

ASSOCHAM said the existing limit of 24 percent investment should be maintained for foreign institutional investors (FIIs). But if their investment has reached the upper limit, they should be allowed to hold non-voting shares in excess of 24 percent.
